why: Here Israel is the nation ("Israel's house", "kings of Israel"), not the patriarch Jacob. Bible Atlas gives Beth-ezel, Shaphir, Zaanan and Maroth one shared point near the coast by Ashdod, but Micah's towns lie along the Judean foothills, so no dot is drawn. Achzib has only a generic point in the foothills, so no dot is drawn either.
Here Israel is the nation ("what is left of Israel"), not the patriarch Jacob.
Here Israel is the nation ("the house of Israel"), not the patriarch Jacob.
This chapter's Plain does not name Israel, so the link does not belong here.

Here Israel is the nation, not the patriarch. Ephrathah in 5:2 is the clan and district around Bethlehem, already linked as a place, not the woman Ephrathah. "The land of Nimrod" is a name for Assyria, not the person Nimrod. Bible Atlas puts that land at Babylon's point, far south of Assyria, so no dot is drawn.

Here Moab is the land and kingdom of Balak, linked as a place, not Moab the son of Lot. Bible Atlas puts this Gilgal in the coastal plain, but the Gilgal in Micah 6:5 is the camp by the Jordan near Jericho (Joshua 4-5), reached from Shittim, so no dot is drawn.

This chapter's Plain does not name Israel, so the link does not belong here. "The River" in 7:12 is the Euphrates by custom, but Bible Atlas's point is in the Syrian desert away from the river, so no dot is drawn.
